evals.prompt: Link all my tunnels so they can see each other
expectations: Calls firewall_link_all_toggle with enabled=1
Confirms Full Mesh is enabled
Explains that all tunnels can now reach each other
Reports rules_dormant and explains that existing tunnel-to-tunnel rules are parked, not deleted, and come back when Full Mesh is turned off

evals.prompt: Open port 443 on my Home Server tunnel to the internet
evals.expected_output: Creates a firewall rule for TCP 443
expectations: Lists tunnels to find Home Server's tunnel token and IP
Calls firewall_rule_add with protocol=TCP, src_ip=0.0.0.0/0, dst_port=443
Uses the correct tunnel IP as dst_ip
If the call returns feature_required (firewall_edit or port_forwarding), explains that firewall rules are a Pro feature and shows upgrade_url instead of retrying

evals.prompt: Only let my MacBook and iPhone see each other, not my other devices
evals.expected_output: Creates bidirectional firewall rules between the two tunnels
expectations: Lists tunnels to find MacBook and iPhone tunnel tokens and IPs
Creates a rule allowing MacBook IP to reach iPhone IP
Creates a rule allowing iPhone IP to reach MacBook IP
Does NOT enable link-all (selective mesh only)

evals.prompt: Show me my current firewall rules
evals.expected_output: Lists all firewall rules and mesh status
expectations: Calls firewall_rule_list (or runs firewall-audit.sh), and with Full Mesh on calls it once per tunnel_token, because without one the answer is rules: null
Calls firewall_link_all_status
Reads rules with a // [] guard (rules is null when empty)
Presents rules in a readable format, showing whether each rule is enabled
Does not print tunnel_token values

evals.prompt: Open port 80 on my new cloud server
evals.expected_output: Adds an inbound TCP 80 rule on the cloud server's tunnel
expectations: Finds the cloud server's tunnel_token (list_tunnels with include_vps=1) and its public address
Calls firewall_rule_add on that tunnel_token with protocol=TCP, src_ip=0.0.0.0/0, dst_port=80 and the server's address as dst_ip
Does not print the tunnel_token

evals.prompt: I'm on the free plan, can my laptop and desktop reach each other?
evals.expected_output: Uses Full Mesh, which every plan has, instead of per-pair rules
expectations: Explains that Full Mesh (firewall_link_all_toggle) is available on every plan, Free included
Explains that individual firewall rules need Pro
Calls firewall_link_all_toggle with enabled=1 after the user agrees

evals.prompt: Add another firewall rule to my cloud server db1 allowing TCP 5432 from 203.0.113.7
evals.expected_output: Uses the server's tunnel_token; handles vps_firewall_limit by showing fix and upgrade_url
expectations: Uses db1's own tunnel_token (from vps_list) and never prints it
Knows that rules on a cloud server's own tunnel work on every plan and do not use the device firewall rule quota
Can read firewall_rules_used and firewall_rules_max from vps_list or vps_get to tell the user how close the server is to its cap
On 409 vps_firewall_limit, shows used, max, fix and upgrade_url, offers to remove an unneeded rule, and does not retry

evals.prompt: Delete the rule that opens port 443 on my homeserver
evals.expected_output: Deletes the rule with all six params copied from the list
expectations: Lists the rules first and confirms with the user before deleting
Calls firewall_rule_delete with all six params: tunnel_token (resolved by name in the shell), protocol, src_ip, src_port, dst_ip, dst_port, sending ALL explicitly where the rule has ALL
On 404 Firewall rule not found, lists the rules again and copies the values exactly instead of guessing
Does not print the tunnel_token
